globalRules.description: All defaults in these templates are synthetic test-case values and must not be treated as source-backed production data or real-user profile data.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Persist source="synthetic_test_case" on every generated answer. Downstream calculators should surface these values only in test fixtures, seed data, preview environments, or explicitly marked synthetic estimate runs.

globalRules.description: Synthetic defaults may allow deterministic calculator execution, but confirmed user or project inputs are required before estimates are promoted beyond placeholder confidence.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Use defaultIsPlaceholder=true and userOverrideAllowed=true. When any sensitive or high-impact field remains synthetic, mark confidenceImpactUntilConfirmed as medium unless the field only affects UI routing or eligibility messaging.

globalRules.description: Tax credits, abatements, exemptions, and valuation preferences should not be merged into cash rebate totals by default.
globalRules.implementationNotes: For tax opportunities, set includeInUserFacingTotalDefault=false unless the product explicitly supports tax benefit monetization assumptions and the user has confirmed tax appetite, taxable status, and relevant local tax profile data.

globalRules.description: Tax-liability, gross-receipts, assessed-value, and local-tax fields are sensitive and should not be collected in first-pass public intake unless needed to explain a materially different estimate path.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Place sensitive fields in tax_profile, organization_profile, property_tax_profile, project_quote, or admin_only steps. Prefer optional advanced estimate controls over mandatory first-screen questions.

globalRules.description: Quantity-based incentives must rely on explicit project quantity fields rather than defaulting to unit_count=1.
globalRules.implementationNotes: Fixtures should include materially non-unit quantities for lighting, EV charging, equipment replacement, and multi-site projects so v2 calculators exercise quantity scaling and override behavior.

profileTemplates.displayName: Normal commercial retrofit with quote and preapproval placeholders

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Provides a generic installed-cost input so quote-based and percentage-of-cost calculators can run end to end.
Separates total project cost from estimated incentive-eligible cost for programs that exclude design, contingency, or non-energy scope.
Exercises quantity scaling for equipment-level calculators and prevents accidental unit_count=1 estimates.
Allows bill-screened eligibility, savings sanity checks, and commercial customer segmentation to be tested.
Supports generic gas-using commercial retrofit scenarios without using real customer utility spend.
Tests estimate status transitions when a quote is available.
Supports stale-quote checks and project timeline logic.
Allows test cases to verify that preapproval messaging appears before installation or purchase.
Prevents synthetic cases from accidentally failing programs that require approval before work begins.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator should produce a deterministic placeholder estimate for non-tax opportunities while clearly marking all major values as synthetic and user-overridable.

warnings: Do not use this profile as a default for real commercial customers.
Quote and cost fields are placeholders and should be replaced by user, contractor, or admin-confirmed values.
Cash rebate outputs may be previewed, but tax-related outputs should remain separated unless a tax profile is confirmed.

profileTemplates.displayName: Nonprofit, school, or public entity with low tax appetite

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Exercises nonprofit, school, and public-sector branching where tax credits may need different treatment than cash incentives.
Tests suppression or alternate display of tax credits for entities that may not directly use income-tax benefits.
Allows tax-credit calculators to distinguish nominal credit value from likely direct usability.
Supports state tax-credit display logic for tax-exempt or low-tax-appetite organizations.
Creates a test hook for routing tax-credit opportunities into a review or education path instead of a cash-equivalent total.
Provides a larger public-sector project value for grant and percentage-of-cost calculations.
Allows grant expected-value flows to test budget-readiness messaging.
Supports school and government procurement branching without implying a real procurement status.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: Cash incentives and grants may produce placeholder values, but tax-credit benefits should be labeled as potentially unusable, transferable, direct-pay-dependent, or requiring tax review.

warnings: Tax-credit values should not be presented as cash rebates for this profile.
Tax-exempt status and direct-pay or transferability treatment require confirmation.
Sensitive tax fields should be optional and placed outside first-pass public intake.

profileTemplates.displayName: Washington solar manufacturer tax abatement profile

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Targets the Washington-specific solar manufacturer tax abatement opportunity.
Confirms that the fixture is exercising manufacturer eligibility rather than a standard building retrofit.
Provides a synthetic eligibility flag for solar manufacturing activity.
Allows tax-abatement calculations to run against a significant synthetic equipment investment.
Exercises sensitive business-size and tax-base branching for manufacturer tax preference scenarios.
Provides a placeholder tax-rate preference input so a calculator can estimate directional abatement value.
Tests allocation of mixed business activity to eligible manufacturing revenue.
Allows the estimate to route to human review or documentation-required status before inclusion in totals.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator may produce a directional tax-preference preview, but it should not include the result in a user-facing total without confirming eligibility, tax classification, registration or filing requirements, and eligible activity allocation.

warnings: This is not a generic solar installation incentive.
Gross receipts and tax-rate fields are sensitive and should be collected only in an advanced tax or organization profile step.
Washington tax classification and eligibility should be verified before showing a firm estimate.

profileTemplates.displayName: Michigan renewable energy renaissance zone company profile

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Targets the Michigan renewable energy renaissance zone opportunity.
Provides the core location-based eligibility flag needed to exercise zone-specific tax preference logic.
Prevents the synthetic case from implying confirmed zone certification while still allowing estimate flow testing.
Exercises eligibility for a renewable energy business rather than a household retrofit.
Provides a synthetic activity classification for renewable energy zone eligibility.
Supports large commercial or industrial renewable energy test cases.
Exercises property-tax preference calculations where local tax rates materially affect results.
Provides a sensitive placeholder for property-tax valuation and abatement testing.
Allows multi-year tax preference logic to be exercised without asserting a real benefit period.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator should use these values to test zone-based tax benefit modeling, but output should remain a review-required estimate until zone location, certification, eligible business activity, local tax rates, and assessed values are confirmed.

warnings: Zone eligibility is location- and certification-dependent.
Local property-tax and assessed-value fields are sensitive and must not be required in first-pass intake.
Any multi-year value should be displayed separately from one-time rebates and marked as tax-profile-dependent.

profileTemplates.displayName: Rhode Island renewable generation property-tax valuation profile

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Targets Rhode Island renewable generation property-tax valuation testing.
Provides an eligibility flag for property-tax valuation treatment tied to renewable generation.
Supports generation-scale tests beyond small residential systems.
Provides a synthetic system value for valuation and local property-tax impact testing.
Exercises comparison between pre-project assessed value and post-project valuation treatment.
Allows the property-tax calculator to test whether renewable generation value should be excluded, capped, or specially valued.
Provides a local-tax placeholder for estimating annual property-tax impact.
Allows fixture routing for local-tax logic while avoiding use of a real customer location.
Routes valuation-sensitive output to needs-property-tax-profile status until assessor treatment is confirmed.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator should estimate a placeholder annual property-tax effect, not a cash incentive. It should require confirmation of assessed values, local rate, system valuation, and assessor treatment before user-facing inclusion.

warnings: Property-tax valuation is not equivalent to a cash rebate.
Assessed-value and local-tax fields are sensitive.
Municipality and assessor treatment should be confirmed before calculating a firm estimate.

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Targets a fixture family where quantity scaling is central to the estimate.
Provides a materially non-unit count so tests fail if calculators silently default to one fixture.
Tests one-for-one replacement quantity handling.
Provides a generic quantity field for v2 calculators that expect unit_count.
Supports savings-based and watts-reduced incentive formulas.
Allows lighting calculators to compute synthetic demand and energy reduction.
Supports annual kWh savings estimates for lighting scenarios.
Allows rebate caps based on project cost to be tested.
Explicitly marks quantity as a primary user-overridable driver for estimate accuracy.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator should scale by 420 fixtures. Any result equivalent to a single-fixture estimate should be treated as a fixture failure.

warnings: This profile is intended to catch quantity-scaling bugs.
The estimate should visibly depend on user-overridden fixture count.
Do not use a hidden unit_count=1 fallback when fixture_count or unit_count is present.

syntheticAnswers.whyIncluded: Provides an alternative quantity-scaling stress case for charger-port and station-count formulas.
Tests station-count scaling for EV charging opportunities.
Tests port-count scaling when incentives are awarded per port rather than per station.
Ensures v2 generic quantity defaults align with charging ports rather than one project.
Allows rate-table logic to distinguish Level 2 charging from DC fast charging.
Supports eligibility branches for public or shared charging access.
Exercises installed-cost caps for EV charging incentive formulas.
Tests whether make-ready costs are included, excluded, or capped separately.
Explicitly flags charger counts as a high-impact user override.

expectedCalculatorBehavior.notes: The calculator should support station-count and port-count formulas and should not collapse the project to a single charger.

warnings: Clarify whether the relevant opportunity pays per station, per port, per connector, or as a percentage of cost.
Make-ready costs may have different eligibility treatment than charger hardware.
This profile is synthetic and should be used to detect quantity-scaling and cap-application errors.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: Washington solar manufacturer tax abatement estimate path
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Covers a tax-preference opportunity that should not behave like a standard solar installation rebate and requires sensitive business-tax inputs.
expectedLimitations: Requires human review before production use.
Gross receipts and tax classification must be confirmed.
Should not be included in default user-facing cash total.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: Michigan renewable energy renaissance zone tax preference case
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Exercises zone-based eligibility, property-tax valuation, and multi-year tax preference handling.
expectedLimitations: Assessed value and local tax rate are sensitive placeholders.
Multi-year estimates should be separated from first-year incentives.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: Rhode Island renewable generation property-tax valuation case
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Covers property-tax valuation logic and prevents the estimator from treating valuation preferences as direct rebates.
expectedLimitations: Should not be included in user-facing cash total by default.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: School or public entity tax-credit display case
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Ensures tax credits are displayed as tax-profile-dependent benefits rather than cash rebates when the entity has low or zero tax appetite.
expectedLimitations: Direct-pay or transferability treatment is not assumed.
Tax-credit values should be visually separated from cash rebates.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: Commercial lighting quantity override stress case
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Catches formulas that incorrectly calculate one fixture instead of hundreds of fixtures.
expectedLimitations: Fixture wattage and operating hours are synthetic.
Should fail validation if unit_count is ignored.

recommendedTestCaseAdditions.title: EV charging station and port quantity override case
recommendedTestCaseAdditions.whyThisCaseMatters: Tests whether EV charging formulas scale by station, port, connector, project cost, or make-ready cost.
expectedLimitations: Requires opportunity-specific definition of eligible unit.
Make-ready eligibility may differ by program.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the estimated total installed project cost?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use the full contractor quote or best available estimate, including equipment, labor, and other installed costs.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed for percentage-of-cost incentives, caps, and quote-readiness status.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What portion of the project cost is eligible for this incentive?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Some programs exclude design, contingency, maintenance, non-energy scope, or unrelated construction costs.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Improves accuracy for incentives that apply only to eligible cost categories.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: How many eligible units are included in the project?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: For example, fixtures, chargers, ports, heat pumps, meters, or other units depending on the project.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Prevents materially wrong estimates from defaulting to one unit.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Have you received a contractor quote for this project?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: A quote can improve estimate accuracy and help determine whether the project is ready for application or preapproval.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Supports quote-dependent estimate confidence and application-readiness routing.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Have you confirmed whether this incentive requires preapproval before purchase or installation?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Many programs require approval before work starts. Starting early can reduce or eliminate eligibility.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Helps prevent ineligible estimates for programs with preapproval requirements.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What type of organization is applying?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Examples include business, nonprofit, school, government, manufacturer, developer, agriculture, or industrial customer.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Determines eligibility and whether tax benefits should be displayed differently from cash incentives.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Is the applicant generally a taxable entity for the relevant tax credit or tax preference?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This can affect whether a tax credit is directly usable. Skip this during first-pass intake unless a tax incentive is being estimated.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed to distinguish tax-credit value from cash-equivalent value, especially for nonprofits, schools, and public entities.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the applicant's estimated annual federal tax liability?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This is sensitive. It should be optional and used only for advanced tax-credit usability estimates.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Tax-liability fields are sensitive and materially affect tax-credit usability.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the applicant's estimated annual state tax liability?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This is sensitive. It should be optional and used only for advanced state tax-credit or tax-preference estimates.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: State tax-liability fields are sensitive and determine whether tax benefits are likely usable.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Does the applicant want to evaluate direct pay, transferability, or another tax-credit monetization path?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This does not confirm eligibility. It helps route the estimate to the right tax-benefit explanation or review step.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed for tax-credit display logic when the applicant may not directly use credits.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What are the applicant's estimated annual gross receipts from relevant business activity?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This is sensitive business information and should be requested only when needed for a tax preference or advanced estimate.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Gross-receipts fields are sensitive and may affect manufacturer tax preference calculations.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What state business tax rate should be used for this estimate?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use only when estimating a tax-rate preference. The actual tax classification should be confirmed by the applicant or advisor.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Local or state business-tax rate assumptions materially affect tax-preference estimates.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What share of the applicant's taxable activity is tied to eligible manufacturing?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use an estimate only for test or preview purposes. Actual allocation may require tax or accounting review.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed for manufacturer-specific tax preference calculations with mixed eligible and ineligible activity.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Does the applicant manufacture solar energy equipment?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This helps determine whether the project should be routed to manufacturer tax-preference logic rather than customer installation incentives.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Core eligibility field for solar manufacturer tax-abatement test cases.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Is the project site located in a qualifying renaissance zone?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Location-based tax preferences usually require confirmation by address, parcel, or official zone documentation.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Core eligibility field for zone-based tax preference estimates.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the applicant's renaissance zone certification status?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use confirmed documentation where available. Otherwise route to human review.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Zone-based tax benefits should not produce firm estimates without certification confirmation.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Which renewable energy business activity applies to this project?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Examples may include manufacturing, development, generation, storage, or related renewable energy business activity.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Determines whether a renewable energy business fits opportunity-specific eligibility rules.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the assessed real property value used for local property-tax purposes?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This is sensitive and should usually come from a property-tax bill, assessor record, or admin-confirmed source.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Assessed-value fields are sensitive and are required for property-tax valuation or abatement estimates.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What was the assessed property value before the renewable generation project?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use only for property-tax valuation estimates. This value should be confirmed before showing a firm estimate.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed to estimate property-tax valuation change while respecting assessed-value sensitivity.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the assessed property value after including the renewable generation project?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use only for property-tax valuation estimates and confirm through assessor or tax records where possible.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed to compare valuation treatment and estimate property-tax impact.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What local property-tax rate should be used for the estimate?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This is sensitive and location-specific. Use a confirmed tax bill, assessor record, or admin-supplied rate for firm estimates.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Local-tax fields are sensitive and materially determine property-tax valuation benefits.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What local real-property tax rate applies to the project site?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use only for advanced property-tax preference estimates and confirm before production use.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Local-tax-rate assumptions are sensitive and high-impact for zone and valuation incentives.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the renewable generation system capacity in kW DC?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use the system design, quote, or interconnection application where available.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Supports renewable generation valuation and eligibility checks.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the fair market value of the renewable generation system?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This may differ from installed cost and should be confirmed for property-tax valuation estimates.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: System value may affect property-tax valuation and should be treated as sensitive property-tax information.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: Has the property-tax assessor treatment been confirmed?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use this to determine whether the valuation estimate can move from placeholder to reviewed.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Property-tax valuation estimates need assessor treatment confirmation before firm user-facing output.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: How many existing lighting fixtures will be replaced or upgraded?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: This quantity can materially change the incentive estimate.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Required for lighting quantity scaling.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the wattage of each existing fixture?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use a typical fixture wattage if exact fixture-level data is unavailable.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Supports savings-based lighting estimates.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the wattage of each new fixture?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Use the product specification or contractor quote when available.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Supports savings-based lighting estimates.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: How many hours per year will this equipment operate?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Operating hours help estimate annual energy savings for lighting and equipment projects.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Improves savings-based estimates and helps test energy-reduction formulas.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: How many EV charging stations are included?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Some incentives pay per station while others pay per port or connector.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Required for EV charging quantity scaling.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: How many EV charging ports are included?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Port count may differ from station count and can materially change the incentive estimate.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Prevents charger estimates from defaulting to one unit or one station when incentives are port-based.

questionCatalogBacklog.questionPrompt: What is the estimated make-ready or electrical infrastructure cost?
questionCatalogBacklog.helperText: Some EV charging incentives treat make-ready costs separately from charger hardware.
questionCatalogBacklog.reason: Needed to test EV charging incentive caps and eligible cost categories.

validationWarnings: output_003_test_case_profile_defaults.md had unescaped source="synthetic_test_case" prose; escaped it before JSON parsing.

implementationNotes: The templates intentionally favor richer reusable profile defaults over patching existing public sample cases.
All syntheticAnswers use source="synthetic_test_case", defaultIsPlaceholder=true, and userOverrideAllowed=true.
The three requested tax-related opportunity IDs are covered by dedicated templates.
Tax benefits, abatements, and property-tax valuation effects are excluded from user-facing totals by default.
Sensitive tax-liability, gross-receipts, assessed-value, and local-tax fields are marked sensitive in the question catalog backlog.
Quantity-scaling stress profiles are designed to expose incorrect unit_count=1 fallbacks.
